rationale: Both documents credit the same source, Raman et al.'s white-bear steering paper (papers/raman2026-white-bear-steering.md), as the closest prior work, and both frame the method's novelty identically: the white-bear effect is treated as a phenomenon to be explained (not a recipe to copy), isolated via the metric server's capture, and re-derived from scratch using definite-referent maintenance rather than concept/suppression, generalizing across referent kinds without using the benchmark's own items. The only minor divergence is that the write-up additionally specifies that the source itself was built from WorkspaceBench's directed_modulation items, a detail the message does not spell out, though it implies the same contrast by stressing its own independence from benchmark items.
